statement: enforcer-config (arc-03) exposes ONLY a read/load API (load_project_config, load_project_tie, parse_project_tie) — there is no store/write function anywhere in the crate. g05's settings mutation route (crates/enforcer-ui/src/settings/write.rs) therefore builds its own write path directly on top of the typed model instead: load the current typed ProjectConfig, mutate policy.rule_toggles via BTreeMap::insert (never append), re-validate the WHOLE merged config through ResolvedProjectTie::resolve before any I/O, then serde_json::to_string_pretty exactly once. No raw string/regex edits of the config file anywhere in the write path.
why: The workpack text says 'writes route ONLY through the arc-03 store API', but no such store API exists yet; a future g05-adjacent lane (or arc-03 itself) may want to formally add ProjectConfig::store()/save() to enforcer-config and have this crate delegate to it instead of owning serialization itself.
howToApply: If/when enforcer-config grows a typed store/save function, replace settings::write::serialize_config + std::fs::write with a call into that function so enforcer-ui goes back to being pure orchestration with zero serialization logic of its own.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-config/src/lib.rs (no store/write fn); crates/enforcer-config/src/project_tie.rs (load_project_tie/parse_project_tie are the only public entry points)

statement: Idempotent config-toggle writes are achieved for free by using BTreeMap::insert keyed on RuleId rather than any append/push operation: ToggleRuleRequest::apply always calls config.policy.rule_toggles.insert(rule_id, RuleToggle{...}), so re-applying the identical request twice replaces the same map entry and produces byte-identical serde_json output both times. Proved by settings::write::tests::retoggling_on_twice_is_byte_identical.
why: The g05 acceptance block explicitly requires re-toggling ON twice to round-trip byte-identical (no duplicated hook/config lines) — this is the mechanical reason it holds, useful for any other lane building a similar toggle-style config mutation (e.g. g04's run-dispatch ledger writes, if it ever needs idempotent re-writes).
howToApply: When building a config/state mutation that must be idempotent under repeated identical calls, prefer a keyed map insert/replace over any list-append, and serialize the whole typed struct through one serde_json call rather than diffing/patching raw text.

statement: g05's settings mutation route is split into a distinct module (crates/enforcer-ui/src/settings/write.rs) from the GET-only read module (crates/enforcer-ui/src/settings/read.rs) specifically so g07's future same-origin/CSRF guard layer can wrap write::toggle_rule alone without touching read::load_settings_view. No function in read.rs performs I/O writes; no function in write.rs is safe to call from a GET handler.
why: g07 (UI-security surface) is a sibling lane that depends on this separation existing per the g05 workpack's own instruction ('keep mutations behind a distinct route module, no mutation on GET') — future g07 work should find write::toggle_rule as the single wrap point.
howToApply: g07: wrap crates/enforcer-ui/src/settings/write.rs's toggle_rule (and any future settings mutation fns added to that module) with the same-origin/CSRF check; do not add checks to read.rs, and do not merge the two modules.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-ui/src/settings/mod.rs module doc comment; crates/enforcer-ui/src/settings/write.rs module doc comment
